scope: Local VanillaMeta public UI and HTTP/WebSocket behavior on develop-v2. Each case must run against a real Nest API and isolated SQLite state unless explicitly labeled fault-injection or provider-contract. A passed DOM-presence smoke test is not proof of numeric correctness or persistence.

oracle.aggregateSql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total FROM uploaded_data
oracle.rowsSql: SELECT id, region, category, amount, qty, name FROM uploaded_data ORDER BY id
oracle.nonMutatingWriteProbe: UPDATE uploaded_data SET amount = amount WHERE 1 = 0
oracle.bigIntSql: SELECT CAST(9007199254740993 AS BIGINT) AS huge FROM uploaded_data LIMIT 1

invariants: Use unique run-owned accounts and resource IDs; never clean up by a broad name prefix on shared state.
Never log credentials or tokens. Generate disposable passwords at runtime; no user secrets or external paid services are used.
Expected aggregate values are the fixed independent oracle above, not values returned by the application or inferred from a successful status code.

A controlled semantic error is a 4xx response or a documented ERROR envelope with a nonempty message and no mutation. Unexpected 5xx, hanging requests, uncaught browser exceptions, and swallowed assertion failures fail the case.

Dashboards are user-associated through UserMapping; unaffiliated users cannot view, edit, delete, or change sharing of another user's private dashboard. Datasources, datasets, widgets, templates, components and metrics currently form a shared authenticated workspace; this task does not invent new ownership columns for them.
Public share and embed pages expose only a currently enabled, unexpired share. Revocation must prevent subsequent reads, including reuse of a previously issued share token.
API-driven setup is permitted, but cases labeled UI must perform their business action through the actual browser UI and verify persisted state independently through API or a fresh browser session.

Do not skip a failing or unavailable scenario to obtain a green total. Report external prerequisites separately. Respect the application's rate limit rather than disabling or raising security controls.

cases.scenario: Anonymous deep links to dashboard, widget, datasource, dataset, metric and file analysis
cases.expected: Each protected route reaches login without rendering private content; root and unknown routes remain responsive.

cases.scenario: Missing, malformed, tampered and expired bearer credentials on every protected controller family
cases.expected: 401 on database, dataset, widget, dashboard, component, template, metric, AI and user info; no private data or mutation.

cases.scenario: Signup required fields, weak password, mismatched confirmation and invalid email
cases.expected: Visible validation error and no signup request or account creation for each invalid input.

cases.scenario: Signup success and onboarding
cases.expected: New runtime-generated account can sign in; its starter dashboard and widgets actually load, including a numeric result, not just a title.

cases.scenario: Duplicate user ID and duplicate email
cases.expected: 409 for each sequential duplicate; original account remains usable and its data is unchanged.

cases.scenario: Wrong password and unknown account
cases.expected: 401 response, visible failure, no token stored, and login page remains usable for a later valid login.

cases.scenario: Login and reload
cases.expected: Authenticated dashboard and profile survive reload; user info omits password and is the correct account.

cases.scenario: Refresh a replaced expired access token using a valid refresh cookie
cases.expected: Actual API refresh succeeds, original data request is retried successfully, no infinite requests or leaked token output.

cases.scenario: Expired access token with no refresh cookie
cases.expected: Authentication is cleared and user reaches login with controlled error, not a blank screen or pending spinner.

cases.scenario: Logout followed by refresh-cookie reuse and protected navigation
cases.expected: Real signout API succeeds, cookie is cleared, saved refresh token cannot renew, browser remains logged out after reload.

cases.scenario: Profile update with wrong current password
cases.expected: Controlled visible failure; email and password remain unchanged and previous login still succeeds.

cases.scenario: Profile password/email update
cases.expected: Updated email persists on fresh profile read; old password fails and new password succeeds after a fresh login.

cases.scenario: Account deletion with wrong and correct password
cases.expected: Wrong password leaves account intact; deleting the run-owned account makes login and refresh fail without 500.

cases.scenario: Corrupt local access-token storage
cases.expected: Malformed stored JSON cannot crash routing; recover to a controlled login state.

cases.scenario: CSV browser analysis
cases.expected: Three rows and six columns from the oracle are visible, aggregate SQL returns exactly 500 and export matches the query result.

cases.scenario: JSON browser analysis
cases.expected: Same three oracle records and aggregate 500 are visible through DuckDB.

cases.scenario: Parquet browser analysis
cases.expected: Same three oracle records and aggregate 500 are visible, not merely a rendered empty canvas.

cases.scenario: Switch bar, line and pie previews
cases.expected: Each selected chart is visibly rendered without uncaught exceptions; data values and selected axes remain correct.

cases.scenario: SQL syntax error followed by valid query
cases.expected: Error is visible, old result is not labeled as a successful new result, and later valid query returns 500.

cases.scenario: Empty query result
cases.expected: No stale rows or chart from the previous query remain; user can run another valid query.

cases.scenario: CSV export with commas, quotes, Unicode and embedded newline
cases.expected: Downloaded CSV round-trips the literal cell values and current result rows correctly.

cases.scenario: Unsafe-integer DuckDB BIGINT result
cases.expected: 9007199254740993 is preserved exactly as text in grid/export; no rounding or BigInt rendering exception.

cases.scenario: Replace uploaded file and analyze again
cases.expected: Only the new file's rows and metadata remain; prior table rows and axis selections do not contaminate results.

cases.scenario: Filename containing apostrophe, spaces and Unicode
cases.expected: Valid CSV is loaded and evaluated successfully; filename quoting cannot break SQL parsing.

cases.scenario: Unsupported file extension and malformed JSON/Parquet
cases.expected: Visible controlled error for each variant, no false success notification, later valid upload works.

cases.scenario: WASM initialization failure and navigation recovery
cases.expected: Explicit engine error and disabled upload while unavailable; navigating away/back with fault removed recovers. This is fault injection, not a live provider test.

cases.scenario: Server CSV, JSON and Parquet upload
cases.expected: Each creates its own SQLite source, reports three rows and executes rowsSql/aggregateSql with exact oracle values.

cases.scenario: Missing, empty, header-only, malformed JSON, non-object JSON array and corrupt Parquet uploads
cases.expected: Each rejected with controlled 4xx; datasource inventory unchanged.

cases.scenario: Unsupported server upload extension
cases.expected: 400 rather than silently interpreting arbitrary extension as CSV; no datasource created.

cases.scenario: CSV BOM, CRLF, quoted comma/newline and escaped quote
cases.expected: Exact header and cell values survive storage and rows query.

cases.scenario: Sanitized colliding headers and duplicate raw headers
cases.expected: Distinct safe column names preserve every original column's values; no silently overwritten cells.

cases.scenario: JSON rows with heterogeneous keys and null/missing values
cases.expected: Union of columns is retained, missing values are null and nonmissing values are not dropped.

cases.scenario: Upload row cap for CSV, JSON and Parquet
cases.expected: 100001 rows rejected rather than truncated; valid three-row input still works afterward.

cases.scenario: Multipart body exceeds 50 MiB
cases.expected: 413 with no metadata source creation, no server crash and subsequent health request succeeds.

cases.scenario: Create a SQLite connection through datasource form
cases.expected: Connection test succeeds for a run-owned uploaded SQLite file, save succeeds and source persists after reload.

cases.scenario: Invalid connection configuration then recovery
cases.expected: Visible test-connection error without success/save claim; valid configuration then succeeds.

cases.scenario: Update source connection after a query initialized its pool
cases.expected: Subsequent query uses the newly selected run-owned file, not the cached old Knex connection.

cases.scenario: Unknown datasource and invalid ID inputs
cases.expected: Controlled non-5xx error for detail/info/query/update/delete paths, no unrelated datasource mutation.

cases.scenario: Valid SELECT, CTE, aggregate and zero-row SQL
cases.expected: Exact oracle rows/500 and empty array respectively; complete response envelope and column metadata.

cases.scenario: Nonmutating UPDATE probe and multiple SELECT statements
cases.expected: 400 from read-only/single-statement guard; later count remains three and sum remains 500.

cases.scenario: SQL syntax error, missing table and empty SQL
cases.expected: Controlled 4xx or ERROR envelope with meaningful message; no 500 or poisoned subsequent valid query.

cases.scenario: Read datasource detail and table/dataset listing
cases.expected: Uploaded_data table is listed; connection password is never returned and datasource is usable.

cases.scenario: File analysis to persisted dataset
cases.expected: Upload through browser, enter aggregateSql in dataset editor, run returns 500, save then fresh API read preserves entered title/query/source.

cases.scenario: Dataset modification
cases.expected: Changed title/query persist after reload and widget data reflects the saved SQL, not old editor state.

cases.scenario: Dataset invalid query and required-title validation
cases.expected: Visible errors, save does not create/update a dataset, existing persisted definition is unchanged.

cases.scenario: Dataset CRUD with valid and invalid SQL
cases.expected: Create/read/update persist correct source/query; invalid update rejected without overwriting prior query; run-owned delete removes record.

cases.scenario: Missing dataset IDs
cases.expected: Controlled errors for detail/update/delete and no unrelated record mutation.

cases.scenario: Delete dataset referenced by a run-owned widget/dashboard
cases.expected: Dependent widget is removed or displayed as an explicit unavailable widget; dashboard remains loadable and no 500/stale successful chart.

cases.scenario: Create, evaluate, reload and delete metric
cases.expected: SUM(amount) value 500 is visible; API evaluate reports SUCCESS/result[0].value=500; deletion removes the active card.

cases.scenario: Missing fields, duplicate active name and cancel creation
cases.expected: Visible validation/duplicate error; no extra active metric and cancel leaves inventory unchanged.

cases.scenario: All six aggregation functions
cases.expected: SUM=500, AVG=500/3, COUNT=3, MIN=100, MAX=250, COUNT_DISTINCT(region)=2 on the fixed oracle. Float comparison is limited to AVG.

cases.scenario: Group-by aggregation
cases.expected: Exactly two rows: 부산=250 and 서울=250, independent of response ordering.

cases.scenario: Filter operators including equality, comparison, LIKE and IN
cases.expected: Known filtered oracle sums/counts; quote-containing values are bound rather than interpolated.

cases.scenario: Invalid definition, unsafe identifier, unsupported aggregation/operator and empty IN values
cases.expected: ERROR with meaningful message, no unsafe execution and no invalid active definition accepted as usable.

cases.scenario: Update metric aggregation and filters
cases.expected: Definition persists, changed evaluation matches oracle and failed update preserves the prior definition.

cases.scenario: Soft delete then recreate same name
cases.expected: One active metric, reused ID allowed; recreated definition and new evaluation are correct, not a duplicate-name failure.

cases.scenario: Deleted/missing metric evaluation
cases.expected: Deleted metric is not usable as an active metric; missing IDs return controlled ERROR and no data.

cases.scenario: Numeric widget wizard
cases.expected: Select the actual oracle source/amount column and numeric component; save, fresh read and view display 500.

cases.scenario: Wizard required selection, back navigation and cancel
cases.expected: Next/save cannot falsely succeed without required choices; back preserves valid inputs; cancel creates no widget.

cases.scenario: Modify widget title and options
cases.expected: Saved title/options and rendered numeric result persist on reload and dashboard view.

cases.scenario: Widget listing and delete confirmation
cases.expected: The created card is visible in the actual list, confirmation cancellation preserves it, confirmed delete removes only its ID.

cases.scenario: Widget TABLE and DATASET creation/update/delete
cases.expected: Correct table-query/dataset linkage; persisted options remain parseable and unrelated widgets are preserved.

cases.scenario: Every enabled registered chart component renders through its real widget view
cases.expected: One variant per enabled componentType, using fresh run-owned widgets and valid explicit option/data fixtures. No fallback component-not-selected message, uncaught exception or empty failed-widget substitute; charts have a real visual surface. Numeric and table variants also assert values. Record each type/screenshot separately; unavailable WebGL is a failure/blocker, not a skip.

cases.scenario: Missing widget deep link and missing underlying datasource
cases.expected: Controlled unavailable/error UI without a blank page or uncaught exception; navigation to a valid widget still works.

cases.scenario: Create dashboard with the numeric oracle widget
cases.expected: Save succeeds, fresh dashboard read preserves widget ID/layout, view displays title and 500.

cases.scenario: Edit dashboard title and add/remove widget
cases.expected: Reload preserves changed title, widget membership and layout; removed widget is not still visible.

cases.scenario: Resize/drag widget and save layout
cases.expected: Layout changes persist on fresh read/reload and widget remains visible without overlap-induced disappearance.

cases.scenario: Dashboard listing, delete cancellation and confirmed deletion
cases.expected: The created dashboard is present in the actual list; cancellation preserves the run-owned dashboard, confirmed delete removes it from list and direct view.

cases.scenario: User-associated dashboard CRUD and partial title-only update
cases.expected: Owner list includes only its own dashboard; title-only update preserves widget membership/layout; delete cleans dependent mappings/sharing and no list 500.

cases.scenario: Second account accesses another user's private dashboard
cases.expected: 403/404 for read/update/delete/share-on/share-off; owner title/layout/share state remain unchanged. Tests use only two new run-owned accounts.

cases.scenario: Unknown and deleted dashboard URLs
cases.expected: Explicit unavailable state, no uncaught errors and no private content.

cases.scenario: Dashboard template-based creation
cases.expected: Recommended template selection yields persisted, usable layout containing the selected widget exactly once.

cases.scenario: Enable sharing in the actual share popup
cases.expected: Real share API succeeds; popup exposes the correct current-origin share/embed URLs and active state persists on reload.

cases.scenario: Anonymous share and embed viewing
cases.expected: Fresh unauthenticated contexts display the correct dashboard and 500; embed omits application navigation.

cases.scenario: Disable sharing and revisit existing share/embed URL
cases.expected: Both anonymous views deny content immediately after revoke, not only after expiry.

cases.scenario: Expired, disabled, unknown and deleted-dashboard shares
cases.expected: Controlled 401/403/404; no private data in responses and no 500.

cases.scenario: Malformed share date and same-day expiry boundary
cases.expected: Malformed input rejected with no mutation; a valid today date remains usable through the local calendar day's end, yesterday is denied.

cases.scenario: Reuse a previously valid share token after revoke
cases.expected: Subsequent datasource reads through that token are denied, and token cannot authorize writes or another dashboard's data.

cases.scenario: Copy link/embed and clipboard-denied behavior
cases.expected: Permitted clipboard contains exact current-origin URL/code; denied clipboard yields visible controlled feedback. Clipboard fault is labeled fault injection.

cases.scenario: Template list/detail/create/update/soft delete
cases.expected: All operations return within bounded timeout; detail has correct layout, update persists and deleted template leaves active list.

cases.scenario: Recommend template and obtain dashboard layout
cases.expected: Valid selected widget is mapped exactly once to finite nonnegative positions/sizes; no missing or duplicate widget mapping.

cases.scenario: Unknown template, empty widget selection and invalid layout input
cases.expected: Controlled non-5xx error/empty recommendation as appropriate; no hanging response or unwanted template creation.

cases.scenario: AI disabled and invalid prompt/ID boundaries
cases.expected: Missing configuration, empty/2001-character prompt and nonpositive IDs yield explicit ERROR without external calls.

cases.scenario: Local OpenAI-compatible SQL response
cases.expected: Local HTTP provider fixture returns the predefined aggregateSql; backend validates it and the real SQLite query yields 500. This does not prove real model quality.

cases.scenario: Provider returns write SQL or multiple statements
cases.expected: Backend returns controlled ERROR, never exposes unsafe SQL as SUCCESS and oracle rows remain intact.

cases.scenario: Provider HTTP error, empty output and malformed payload
cases.expected: Controlled error for each variant and subsequent normal request recovers; no external paid calls.

cases.scenario: Valid and invalid chart recommendation types
cases.expected: Registered CHART_BAR is accepted; invented type and malformed JSON are rejected rather than silently chosen.

cases.scenario: Dashboard insight with valid, missing and empty dashboards
cases.expected: Valid fixture insight is displayed/returned; missing/empty context gives controlled error, not fabricated success.

cases.scenario: Dataset AI SQL assistant
cases.expected: Real browser action against local provider inserts the exact SQL into editor and Run yields 500; error fixture displays feedback and leaves prior valid SQL intact.

cases.scenario: Dashboard AI insight action
cases.expected: Real action displays the known local provider fixture text; unavailable provider error is visible. No claim about model reasoning correctness.

cases.scenario: WebSocket query progress success and error
cases.expected: Own socket receives running then success/error for real SQLite requests; successful row count is three; a second unrelated socket receives no event.

cases.scenario: Optional in-memory cache enabled and TTL expiration
cases.expected: Repeated identical queries are stable; after changing a run-owned datasource connection and expiry, results use new data. Cache configuration belongs only to a dedicated local process.

cases.scenario: Rate limit and recovery
cases.expected: Actual configured limit produces 429, not 500; after its window the same local server returns normally. Do not raise/disable the limit to pass other tests.

cases.scenario: Transient API network error and later recovery
cases.expected: Visible feedback, loading overlay clears, no uncaught exception and retry/navigation reaches working state. Fault injection is explicitly labeled.

cases.scenario: Fresh local bootstrap and restart persistence
cases.expected: Automatic seed and new CRUD resources are usable through public API; restarting same isolated DB preserves exact fixture values, resource IDs and account access without duplicate seed rows.

cases.scenario: Corrupt encrypted connection config does not take down source/dashboard listing
cases.expected: A deliberately corrupted run-owned config produces explicit item error, healthy sources/dashboard remain loadable; repair restores usability. This fixture is never inserted into user data.

cases.scenario: Korean/English language switch and reload
cases.expected: Visible navigation/page text actually switches and persisted language survives reload; test cannot silently pass when selector is absent.

cases.scenario: Phone and tablet viewport navigation
cases.expected: Login, datasource/metric page and dashboard are operable at 390x844 and 768x1024 with reachable controls and no uncaught exceptions.

cases.scenario: Missing route, browser back/forward and deep-link reload
cases.expected: Correct page/not-found state, no blank application or unintended loss of authenticated navigation.

cases.scenario: Create/edit cancellation and unsaved navigation
cases.expected: No unwanted resource creation or persisted changes from cancellation; user can return to a valid page.

cases.scenario: Component create/read/update/delete on a new run-owned type
cases.expected: Update changes the original ID rather than inserting a new record; delete removes only the created type; options remain parseable.

cases.scenario: Duplicate component type and missing component ID
cases.expected: Controlled conflict/error without new duplicate rows, server error or unrelated mutations.

externalPrerequisites.status: requires isolated real server and explicit connection provisioning
externalPrerequisites.rule: Local SQLite and HTTP provider fixtures are not evidence these external services work.

externalPrerequisites.status: requires model provisioning and approved service use
externalPrerequisites.rule: Contract fixtures verify integration and error handling only, never model accuracy.
Memory-cache tests do not certify Redis persistence or multi-instance consistency.
